header_sentences: See Learned; and see Instruct, Prophet, and Shepherd.

contexts.text: Who is blinder than those who love themselves and at the same time are learned from the world? Described. AC 946.
The order of teaching and learning in the Word commences from the most general things.
The most learned are in greater unbelief than the simple. AC 1636, Example AC 1911:5. AC 3348:3, Example(s). AC 3482:end. AC 3677:2.
As streets = truths, it was a representative rite among the Jews to teach in them. Illustrated.
The third kind of men in the Church are those who know truths, but are in evil. These are signified by the sons-in-law of Lot. They are especially those who teach. Described.
That thus it would be taught. Signified, Explained. AC 2538. Explained.
A prophet = one who teaches; abstractedly, the doctrine itself. Illustrated. AC 3316:4.
The Angels perceive nothing more blessed and happy than to teach novitiate brethren...
The rider (who falls backward) = one who teaches.
False prophets = those who teach falsities.
Hence to hunt = to teach, and also to persuade; and this in both senses, from the affection of truth, and from the affection of falsity. Illustrated.

Fishers = those who teach from sensuous truths; hunters, those who teach from scientific truths and doctrinals. Upon every mountain, and upon every hill = to teach those who are in the affection of good, and in the affection of truth.
From this may be evident the quality at this day of those who teach others.
They who teach truths... and live evilly... at heart do not believe.
Unless... teaching good is conjoined with thinking good, there is no good in the man; for the evil can... think evil and teach good.
As the Lord does not inflow immediately with man, and teach him; but inflows into his Knowledges...
The Subjects who appear above, and near, the head, are those who teach, and also suffer themselves to be easily taught.
The Lord inflowed by an internal way with (the Most Ancients), and taught them what is good... (But the Ancient Church was taught by representatives; and the Christian, by doctrinals.)
That He was present with those who... taught. Signified, Explained.
To pasture the flock = to teach, in special from doctrinals, those in the Church.
To prophesy = to teach and preach truths, or falsities. Illustrated.
Binding sheaves = teaching from doctrine.
That (the Lord's Divine Spiritual) should teach Divine spiritual goods. Signified, Explained.
He who teaches Divine spiritual goods, teaches also Divine spiritual truths; for the latter are from the former and are about them.
To be sent = to proceed, and to teach. Illustrated. AC 4715.
Every coming of the Lord, and the perception how it was with those who taught. Signified, Explained.

That He taught the lower things of the Church, because they did not comprehend the higher ones. Signified, Explained... For he who teaches faith, and not charity, cannot perceive the more interior things of the Church. Explained... But if he teaches charity, he has good, and this is a dictate to him, and guides him...
It is said of the celestial, that they are taught from the Lord's Divine Rational. Explained.
Joseph's brethren, being shepherds, = those who teach from faith separated.

For the doctrinals of faith... if separated from those of charity, teach almost nothing. For the doctrinals of charity teach what good is; and the doctrinals of faith teach what truth is; and to teach truth without good is to walk as one who is blind, because good is what teaches and leads, and truth is what is taught and led. There is as great a difference between these two doctrinals as between light and darkness...
To teach the bow () = to teach the doctrine of love and charity. See AC 9468:4. AE 357:3.
For faith without charity, or truth without good, teaches nothing...
That the Celestial of the Natural taught them from things primary for interpretation. Signified, Explained.
For the Lord does not openly teach anyone truths; but He leads them through good to think what is true...
They who teach, and are in evils: that they set themselves in opposition. Signified, Explained.
I will teach thee what thou shalt say () = ... to proceed; for to teach, and to speak, = to inflow; and, when predicated of the Divine of the Lord, to proceed... AC 7007.
I will teach you what ye shall do () = thus the Divine [shall be] in each and all things which shall be done.
The mediate influx of Divine truth into doctrine, that is, with one who teaches. Signified.
Pass over before the people = that he should lead and teach them.
He who teaches, leads in a spiritual way.

By revelation is meant illustration when the Word is being read, and perception then; for they who are in good, and long for truth, are taught in this way from the Word; whereas they who are not in good cannot be taught from the Word, but only confirmed in such things as they have been instructed in from infancy...
That they are taught (from revealed truth) what is true and what is good. Signified, Explained.
To make known = to teach.
To tempt you = to teach that there is a life of Heaven and the nature of it; for all spiritual temptation teaches and confirms such things with man. Explained.

Among priests, and among the men of the Church, there are some who teach and learn the truths of the Church from the literal sense... and some who teach and learn from doctrine from the Word. (Continued. See Doctrine.)
Those are sorcerers who are learned from themselves... Illustrated. For he who would be learned in the truths and goods of faith, must be learned (or taught) from the Lord.
Diviners, etc. = ... thus those who learn and teach from a cupidity for gain and honours, and not from the affection of the truth of faith and the good of life.
Therefore mention is made of a Prophet who shall come and teach.
People are taught by the Lord while they are reading the Word, not for the sake of self and the world, but for the sake of what is good and true itself; for they are then illustrated...
The like is the case with those who teach: they are heard in Heaven as crying out.
To sow the land, or a field = to teach and learn the truths and goods of faith which are of the Church. Illustrated.
To teach truths not genuine. Signified.
Teachers = those who instruct.
Which I will write to teach them () = for remembrance and information.
To teach the truths of doctrine from a celestial origin. Signified.
To judge judgment = to teach Divine truth.
As faith without charity does not love the Lord, and yet can teach such things as are of faith and love... the Lord said three times, Lovest thou me; Feed my lambs...
Those who believe they are more learned than others, and yet are in falsities. Treated of.
Thus He instructeth him to judgment; his God teacheth him () = ... to give him intelligence, and to give him wisdom...
Under Priest, see this reference. AC 10798.
See Preacher.
The lot of those who study knowledges merely to be thought learned.
The Lord teaches everyone through the Word; and He teaches from those truths which the man has, and does not pour in new ones immediately...
Thus the Lord is the most present in the sense of the letter, and from it teaches and illustrates man. DSS 53.

There is a spiritual idea... which inflows with those who are in the affection of truth, and which dictates interiorly that what is heard, or read, is true, or not... These are they who are called taught by Jehovah (; ); and who are spoken of in .
(The effect on others of a) lack of truth with those who teach.
The Spirits who of the Lord's permission speak with man, never... teach: the Lord alone teaches man, but mediately through the Word, in illustration. From experience.
That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man be led and taught by the Lord from Heaven through the Word, doctrine, and preachings from it; and this in all appearance as of himself. Chapter.

It is from the appearance that man is led and taught by himself; but it is from the Truth that he is led and taught by the Lord alone. They who confirm the appearance with themselves... cannot remove from themselves evils as sins...
The Lord gives these to interiorly perceive that they are not led and taught by themselves, but by the Lord.
That man is led and taught by the Lord alone. General article.
That man is led and taught by the Lord alone is because he lives from the Lord alone; for the will of his life is led, and the life of his understanding is taught. Explained.
That man is led and taught by the Lord alone through the angelic Heaven and from it. General article.
That man is led by the Lord by influx, and is taught by illustration. General article.
It follows that the man who is taught from the Word, is taught by the Lord alone. Explained. DP 172:5.
But everyone is taught according to the understanding of his love: what goes beyond this, does not remain.

All who are taught by the Lord in the Word, are taught a few truths in the world, but many when they become Angels; for the interiors of the Word... are simultaneously implanted, but are not opened with the man until after his death...

The Word cannot be taught otherwise than mediately, through parents, masters, preachers, books, and especially through the reading of it; but still it is not taught by these agencies; but through them by the Lord.
That in external things man is led and taught by the Lord in all appearance as of himself. Explained.

These... are led by the Lord; and they who are led, are also taught, according to their religion, concerning God and the neighbour; for they who so live love to be taught; but they who live otherwise do not; and, as they love to be taught, they are instructed by the Angels after death...
The Truth, and the study of acquiring and teaching it. Signified, Explained.
For all who have fought against evils... and have believed in the Lord, are taught by Him after their departure from the world...
That the Lord alone will teach them. Signified, Explained.
That to feed = to teach. Illustrated.
We, said they, are the purple-clad doctors.
That... these two essentials of the New Church are to be taught until the end and the beginning. Signified, Explained. AE 636.
That they speak, teach, and write from the Word... and yet it is truth falsified. Signified, Explained.
That no one is permitted (by the solifidians) to teach from the Word... but those who acknowledge that doctrine... Signified, Explained. AE 840.
The understanding so closed that man can scarcely be taught any longer. Signified, Explained.
That they should let down the net on the right side of the ship... = that they should teach the good of charity, and in that way they would gather men.
They who teach false and heretical things... and yet read the Word, and are able to know from it what is false and what is true... may be compared to impostors...
On the teachableness of Spirits... Spirits are easily taught. Example(s).
That no one claims anything in Heaven because he has taught many things (here).
An intense love of teaching; its motives.

No Spirit is allowed to teach man, and consequently not to lead him, except from cupidity; but the Lord alone wills to teach and lead man; which would not be possible if a Spirit possessed anything of the corporeal memory.
A certain doctor of great dignity who supposed himself to be more learned than others...
Women can give utterance with affection, and thus excite to what is devout and holy; but cannot teach.
Men who teach... have two states; one when they teach and think from doctrine; and the other when they are thinking outside of doctrine. Explained.
To teach, and to seduce My servants ()... To teach is predicated of truths, or falsities.
This delight (of the love of self and the world) teaches and seduces those who are in truths.
To be taught in the streets ()-to know the things which must be of faith.
The sons who shall be taught of Jehovah... () = those who in the New Heaven and New Church will be in truths from good from the Lord.
Those who teach falsities and through them lead to evil of life. Signified.
The teacher of a lie () = one who teaches falsity by applying scientifics from the sense of the letter to confirm falsities.
Instruction in the truths of doctrine, is signified by, Thine eyes shall look again to thy teachers (). Teachers = doctrine.

Be not ye called Rabbi; one is your teacher, Christ (). Rabbi, and teacher = one who teaches truth; thus, in the abstract, the doctrine of truth; and, in the supreme sense, the Divine truth, which is Christ. (Thus these words mean) that the Lord alone is the Divine truth. AE 746:13.
Teach me Thy way, Jehovah () = to teach the truth according to which we are to live.
That they will be taught in truths by which they will be led, is signified by, He will teach us of His ways, and we shall go in His paths ().
When Thou teachest the earth Thy judgments, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness () = that the Church is in truths from the Lord, and, through truths, in good.
For the Lord is the teacher of all... and from Him as the teacher is all the truth of that good.
Only abstain from evils as sins, and look to the Lord, and the Lord will teach and lead.

The ninth law of the Divine Providence is, That the Lord does not teach man truths immediately, either from Himself or through the Angels; but that He teaches mediately through the Word, preachings, readings, speech and intercourse with others, and thus by thoughts in ourselves therefrom. Explained. AE 1177, Explained.
Who do not want to learn, but to teach.
These are more teachable than the rest.

Leave is granted to no Spirit, or Angel, to teach any man in this Earth Divine truths; but the Lord Himself teaches everyone through the Word, and He teaches him in the proportion that he receives from the Lord good in the will; and he receives it in proportion as he shuns evils as sins. Explained.
